senses.definition: (intransitive, transitive) To admit to the truth, particularly in the context of sins or crimes committed.
examples: I confess to spray-painting all over that mural!
I confess that I am a sinner.

quotes.text: I never gave it him. Send for him hither, / And let him confess a truth.
quotes.reference: c. 1603–1604 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Othello, the Moore of Venice”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene ii]:

quotes.text: And there confess / Humbly our faults, and pardon beg.
quotes.reference: 1667, John Milton, “Book IX”, in Paradise Lost. quotes.text: I must confess I was most pleased with a beautiful prospect that none of them have mentioned.

senses.definition: (transitive) To acknowledge faith in; to profess belief in.

quotes.text: Whosoever, therefore, shall confess me before men, him will I confess, also, before my Father which is in heaven.

senses.definition: (religion) To unburden (oneself) of sins to God or a priest, in order to receive absolution.

quotes.text: If we confesse our sinnes, hee is faithfull, & iust to forgiue vs our sinnes, and to cleanse vs from all vnrighteousnesse.

quotes.text: Our beautiful votary took an opportunity of confessing herself to this celebrated father.
